abstract_summary: Long-running LLM agents require memory that persists and evolves across sessions. Text-based memory retrieves and reconstructs past interactions at every query, making long-horizon performance increasingly dependent on retrieval quality and contextual reasoning as histories grow. Parametric memory encodes experience...

Benchmarks and metrics.PERMA [ 25] evaluates memory formation, revision, and intervention across
ordered sessions; we report its four clean and noisy single-domain (SD) and multi-domain (MD) settings and
their macro-average. PersonaMem-v2 [3] derives independent queries from long user histories; we report
Overall, Self, and Current accuracy. PrefEval [2] measures memory after 10, 70, and 300 intervening turns,
averaged across its three information forms. Detailed task construction and metric definitions appear in
Appendix D.1.
Baselines.Textual-memory methods include Full Context, RAG [26] with M3-Embedding [27], Rolling
Summary, Mem0 [8], and LightMem [9]. Parametric baselines include SFT, trained on the same downstream
split with the visible history, and the released Metis-9B recurrent-memory model [16]. No Context and
Gold State provide query-only and annotated-memory references.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are measured with objective multiple-choice accuracy on held-out benchmark partitions, including leave-one-user-out PERMA folds, PersonaMem-v2 test questions, and topic-held-out PrefEval, which do not reuse the compiler or gate training signals.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Final evaluation uses exact answer-label accuracy on held-out benchmark partitions: PERMA ten-fold leave-one-user-out, PersonaMem-v2 benchmark split, and PrefEval held-out topics.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The compiler is trained by forward-KL matching against frozen context-conditioned teacher distributions, and the consolidation gate is trained with answer-token cross-entropy on task training splits.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding lifecycle independence, improved cross-session accuracy over baselines, constant per-session write latency, and cross-backbone transfer are fully supported by empirical tables and dynamics analyses.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is evaluated extensively across three distinct agent memory benchmarks (PERMA, PersonaMem-v2, and PrefEval) and five LLM backbones, comparing against strong textual-memory and parametric baselines. Thorough ablations confirm the utility of the forward-KL objective and coordinate-wise learned gating, alongside operational efficiency profiling and general-capability retention tests.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on objective discrete multiple-choice accuracy metrics across benchmark partitions with held-out users, topics, and distinct tasks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Final evaluation measures exact accuracy on standard held-out multi-choice test benchmarks (PERMA 10-fold leave-one-user-out, PersonaMem-v2 test partition, and topic-held-out PrefEval).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The memory compiler is trained via forward-KL distribution matching against frozen context-conditioned teacher distributions on synthetic and dialog datasets, and the recurrent gate is trained using answer-token cross-entropy loss on task training splits.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly note that consolidation gates are trained per application scenario, leaving cross-scenario transfer and generalization across tasks with divergent memory requirements for future work.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the Perceiver-based resampler and LoRA decoder trained via fixed-reference forward-KL distillation, followed by cross-session consolidation using a lightweight recurrent gate trained on downstream task supervision while holding the rest of the architecture frozen.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-engineered, and comprehensive evaluation of a parametric memory architecture with extensive ablation studies, cross-architecture generalization, and diagnostic analysis of consolidation dynamics.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RPMem, a two-stage parametric memory framework that compiles individual interaction sessions into a fixed-shape model-independent latent space and updates an evolving memory state via a task-supervised recurrent gate before decoding into model-specific LoRA parameters.
